name: Burns & McDonnell
legalName: Burns & McDonnell (100% employee-owned via ESOP; no outside shareholders)
employees: 14,000+ (company, 2024); 75+ offices worldwide incl. a 1,900+ person India subsidiary
summary: BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT: Burns & McDonnell is the AI buildout's utility-side capture play — ENR's #1 power design firm eleven consecutive years, claiming the largest substation design group in the country and >50% US market share in reciprocating-engine (RICE) power plants, fused to a Tier-3 data-center design-build practice under one 100% employee-owned (ESOP) roof. Record 2025 revenue of $8.6B (+19%, after an unexplained ~3% dip to $7.2B in 2024) rode what ENR's 2026 cover story calls the AI design boom, and the Santee Cooper award is the template: a single Aiken County, SC data center generated a utility transmission EPC (16 miles of 115 kV rebuild, two new 230 kV lines, a new 230 kV substation) — Burns & McDonnell gets paid on the utility side of the meter, where competition is thinnest. The design-led hybrid position is distinctive: #7 on ENR's Top 500 Design Firms but #35 on the Top 400 Contractors, after construction revenue grew ~300% under prior CEO Ray Kowalik. Leslie Duke — a T&D-native engineer and the firm's first female president — became Chair and CEO January 2024. Watch items: an active January 2026 lawsuit (Certus Cybersecurity v. 1898 & Co.) alleging MWBE-commitment abuse on a $60M Seattle City Light contract, and the structural cash constraint every aging ESOP carries (repurchase obligations, no outside capital). Collection gap: no backlog or profitability disclosure; revenue is company-stated alongside annual ENR rankings.
ecosystemRole: The power-first engineer of the AI buildout: designs (and increasingly builds) the substations, transmission, grid interconnections, and bridge generation that hyperscale campuses force onto utilities — then sells the data center building itself as an integrated design-build package.

productsAndServices.name: Mission Critical / Data Center Design-Build
productsAndServices.description: Site selection through commissioning for data centers, switch centers, control rooms, SCIFs, and DoD facilities — architecture, engineering, construction, and commissioning 'under one roof,' fast-track and turnkey. The practice was rebuilt around design-build, modular construction, and prefabrication after the 2021 hire of mission-critical leader David Bals, and has been adapted for AI densities including advanced thermal management and liquid cooling (Tier 3 / TIA-942 baseline).
highlights: The integration pitch: on-site generation, bridging power, utility interconnection, long-lead equipment procurement, and phased EPC substation delivery aligned to load ramp — the data center AND its power delivered as one package
Wyoming Hyperscale: company-named 'world's first sustainable hyperscale data center ecosystem' construction launch; hyperscaler client names otherwise undisclosed (NDA norms)
Independent datapoint: a >$100M, 150,000 sq ft Temple, TX data center on 1,200 concrete piers with up to 185 MW draw, completed summer 2023
White-paper canon markets storage-as-core-power-strategy and reciprocating engines for data-center demand — Northern Virginia power demand cited up ~500% in a decade
productsAndServices.positioning: Not competing on shell-construction scale with Turner/HITT/Holder — competing on the power interface, where its #1 power-design franchise gives it the seat the building GCs must subcontract
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Design-build/EPC and design-services contracts; NDA-heavy direct hyperscaler and developer relationships
productsAndServices.roadmap: AI-density retrofits (liquid cooling), phased substation-matched delivery, bridge-power integration

productsAndServices.name: Electrical Transmission & Distribution + Substations
productsAndServices.description: The crown jewel: full-scope T&D — AC/DC transmission (overhead, underground, undersea), substations including gas-insulated, generation interconnections, grid modernization (distribution automation, microgrids, non-wires alternatives) — for IOUs, municipals, co-ops, developers, and the military. ENR has ranked Burns & McDonnell #1 in Power design revenue for eleven consecutive years, and the company claims the largest substation design group in the country.
highlights: Santee Cooper / Aiken County SC: transmission EPC built solely to power one data center — ~16 mi of 115 kV rebuilt, two new 230 kV lines, new 230 kV substation (completion late 2025)
The interconnection franchise now applies directly to hyperscaler loads as FERC's 2025-26 large-load interconnection orders expand exactly this work
India T&D group: 400+ engineers in Bengaluru/Mumbai supporting 70 global client teams — offshore design leverage its builder rivals lack
productsAndServices.positioning: Perennial #1 vs Black & Veatch (#2 in power design seven straight years) and Sargent & Lundy (#3); designs what Quanta and Kiewit often build
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Utility framework agreements, EPC and design-services contracts
productsAndServices.roadmap: Data-center-driven utility transmission programs; grid-modernization spend

productsAndServices.name: Electric Power Generation (Gas, RICE, Renewables & Storage)
productsAndServices.description: 1,200+ staff on natural-gas generation with a claimed >50% US market share in reciprocating-engine (RICE) plants — 28 projects in 15 years — plus single-contract EPC for solar, wind, storage, hydrogen, and offshore-wind integration. RICE fleets are the exact 'rapid response power' product AI load centers now need as bridge generation.
highlights: Basin Electric Pioneer Phase IV (Bakken): 600 MW gas expansion — 2 Siemens STG6-5000F simple-cycle turbines + 6 Wärtsilä W18V50SG recip engines
Vistra Moss Landing BESS expansion (350 MW / 1,400 MWh) won ENR Best Project honors (2024)
productsAndServices.positioning: The RICE claim (>50% share, company figure, unverified) would make it the incumbent in the fastest-mobilizing power class for data-center bridge power
productsAndServices.soldThrough: EPC contracts with utilities, co-ops, and IPPs
productsAndServices.roadmap: Storage-as-core-power-strategy for next-generation data centers (its own white-paper thesis)

productsAndServices.name: 1898 & Co. (Consulting, Grid Analytics & Industrial Cybersecurity)
productsAndServices.description: The firm's consulting/digital arm: asset planning and management (including T&D planning), business strategy, data/analytics/AI, enterprise technology, industrial cybersecurity (OT security, managed security services, cyber-informed engineering), financial analysis, and regulatory work for critical-infrastructure clients.
highlights: Extends the engineering franchise into recurring advisory and managed-security revenue
Now the named defendant unit in the Certus Cybersecurity MWBE lawsuit over a $60M Seattle City Light contract (active, allegations only)
productsAndServices.positioning: A Burns & McDonnell-branded answer to the consulting layers at AECOM/Jacobs, differentiated by OT/grid depth
productsAndServices.roadmap: Grid analytics and OT-security demand scaling with electrification

productsAndServices.name: Aviation, Federal, Water & Industrial (diversified book)
productsAndServices.description: The balance of the practice: aviation and federal (the Kansas City KCI single-terminal airport was its landmark design-build), water and wastewater (including the De Soto, KS treatment-plant doubling that serves the Panasonic EV-battery plant site), environmental, transportation, telecom (#3 ENR telecom), and oil & gas/industrial process (#4 ENR).
highlights: ENR 2026 category ranks (company-cited): #3 Telecommunications, #4 Industrial Process/Oil & Gas, #9 Manufacturing
De Soto wastewater doubling opened June 2026 — infrastructure-for-manufacturing adjacency
US Best Managed Company five consecutive years (Gold Honoree 2026)
productsAndServices.positioning: Cycle ballast and public-sector presence around the power/mission-critical core
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Design-build and design-services contracts, public procurement
productsAndServices.roadmap: Steady-state; growth capital concentrates on power and mission-critical

strategyRead: 1. (High confidence) We assess Burns & McDonnell's AI-cycle strategy is utility-side capture rather than shell construction: the #1 power-design rank (11 straight years), the claimed largest US substation design group, and the Santee Cooper template — where one data center generated a full utility transmission EPC — position it to monetize hyperscale growth on the regulated side of the meter, where design authority matters more than construction scale and the building GCs cannot follow.

2. (High confidence) We assess the firm is a design-led EPC hybrid by deliberate construction: #7 designer but #35 (and climbing) contractor, with construction revenue up ~300% across the Kowalik era. The integrated pitch — data center, substation, interconnection, and bridge generation under one P&L — is the differentiation against both pure designers (Sargent & Lundy) and pure builders (Quanta, Kiewit).

3. (Moderate confidence) We assess the RICE franchise (28 reciprocating-engine projects in 15 years; company-claimed >50% US share) is becoming disproportionately valuable: fast-start engine fleets are the default bridge-power answer for AI campuses stuck in interconnection queues, and the firm's own white-paper canon shows it is selling that thesis to data-center clients now. The share claim is unverified — treat the number, not the trend, with caution.

4. (Moderate confidence) We assess the 2024 revenue dip (-3%) followed by 2025's +19% record confirms rising AI/power-capex beta in the book: the firm is increasingly levered to a single demand cycle, partially hedged by aviation, water, federal, and the manufacturing-reshoring adjacency (De Soto/Panasonic).

5. (Moderate confidence) We assess the ESOP is both the moat and the constraint: 100% employee ownership underwrites the retention story in a craft- and engineer-scarce market, but repurchase obligations to an aging 14,000-person workforce consume cash that public rivals deploy into acquisitions and fleets — Quanta buys companies; Burns & McDonnell must grow organically. The 2009-11 Titus ESOP settlement (~$1.2M) is the only public crack in an otherwise clean ownership record.

6. (Low confidence) We assess the Certus/1898 & Co. MWBE lawsuit as contained but non-trivial: allegations of reneging on diversity-partnership commitments in public procurement strike at the trust that wins utility and municipal frameworks. No adjudication exists; an adverse finding would be a real reputational event in exactly its best market.
